briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 30, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Global Climate Catastrophe: Nepal's Great Flood and the Warning of Glacier Collapse
sections.content: The massive floods in Nepal, resulting in 768 deaths and 3,048 missing persons, clearly demonstrate the severity of the global climate catastrophe [58, 59]. With the area of Himalayan glacial lakes surging by 27% and permafrost weakening identified as contributing factors, the phenomenon of 'glacial tsunamis' – where massive walls of water engulf areas even without heavy rainfall – is being observed, indicating a changing pattern of disasters [1, 13, 19, 61]. Experts and Nepal's Foreign Minister have characterized these massive floods as a 'climate backlash,' urging proactive preparedness for climate disasters and global efforts to combat climate change [4, 7, 10, 65, 71, 73]. Furthermore, record-breaking heatwaves in Europe and the strengthening El Niño phenomenon are intensifying concerns that climate change-induced disasters will increase globally [21, 68, 72].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Domestic Carbon Neutrality Efforts: Efforts by Local Governments and Citizens
sections.content: Domestically, local governments and civil society are actively continuing their efforts to achieve a carbon-neutral society [22, 40]. Through its Carbon Neutrality Point System, Siheung City has reduced 4,388 tons of carbon dioxide and provided 39.2 million KRW in incentives over the past year, continuously encouraging citizens to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in their daily lives [16, 24, 28, 36, 37, 38, 39, 42, 45, 46]. Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), as the first public enterprise, is strengthening carbon neutrality and ESG management by creating a 'sea forest' in Gungsi-do, Taean [25, 29, 34], and Busan City has also allocated 4.5 billion KRW for its Climate Response Fund, emphasizing the expansion of carbon-neutral investments [26]. Additionally, various regions are expanding education and participation for carbon neutrality implementation, including the launch of the National Youth Environmental Guardians, the operation of the Gwangmyeong 7-dong Carbon Neutrality Village School, and the Nowon-gu Citizens' Declaration [27, 30, 31, 32, 33, 35]. These efforts demonstrate that environmental protection can lead to economic value creation, similar to Daegu City's case of generating 1.2 billion KRW in revenue through greenhouse gas reduction [41, 44].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Strengthening Climate Change Adaptation and Research Capabilities: Agriculture, Education, and International Cooperation
sections.content: Adaptation efforts to climate change are particularly prominent in the agricultural sector. Jeongseon County is enhancing its response capabilities by upgrading agricultural weather observation equipment to establish climate change-tailored 'smart farming' [2, 12, 14, 15], and the case of a farm that has supplied potatoes resilient to climate change for 37 years demonstrates the importance of adaptive agriculture [8, 20]. In the education sector, Chungcheongnam-do is making inclusive efforts for the socially vulnerable by expanding 'educational access rights' for people with disabilities in climate crisis education [3]. Furthermore, international solidarity is strengthening, with Ulsan College collaborating with Uzbekistan's Green University in environmental and climate change fields [6], and a proposal to combine ancient knowledge with modern science to address climate change is also noteworthy [75]. Meanwhile, NASA is expanding the horizons of climate and space science research by launching a powerful new Roman Space Telescope from Florida [79].

sections.title: ⚠️ Realities and Policy Challenges of Energy Transition: The Dual Nature of Renewable Energy
sections.content: Complex challenges are emerging in the domestic energy transition process. The National Human Rights Commission urged the revision of the Carbon Neutrality Act to an early intensive reduction pathway, pointing out that current reduction targets may be insufficient [23]. The 'paradox of the demonstration island,' where Jeju Island, with 65% of its power generation from renewable energy, is excluded from industrial electricity bill discounts, suggests the need for policy improvements [53, 56]. Furthermore, ecosystem disruption issues are severe, such as the spread of vines due to climate change leading to secondary pest control in Jeju City [17], and the voices of glacier and climate change researchers expressing concerns about increasing disasters are also growing [4, 72]. The case of West Point's only climate scientist being fired for teaching 'human-caused climate change' illustrates international difficulties in climate science education and information dissemination [69], and the efforts of Boeun rice farmers to find solutions while facing climate change and rising production costs represent the realistic challenges in the agricultural sector [11].

briefing.closing: This concludes today's climate briefing for August 30, 2026. We look forward to seeing you again at the next briefing.
